CenterOfMassConfig.description:
Configuration for the `CenterOfMassRefiner`.

Controls the size of the weighted-centroid window. The centroid is
computed over a `(2·radius+1)²` patch on the ChESS response map
centered at the rounded seed position.

radius.description:
Half-width of the centroid window, in response-map pixels (integer
`>= 0`; the window is `(2·radius+1)²`). Default `2` (a 5×5 window);
larger values smooth single-pixel noise but may merge energy from
nearby corners.

Advanced tuning. The default is appropriate for most scenes.

ChessConfig.description:
Configuration for the ChESS detector branch of `DetectionStrategy`.

Carries the detector ring choice and the tuning of ChESS's own subpixel
localizer. The shared NMS / clustering thresholds
(`DetectionParams`), multiscale, upscale and the optional image
refiner (`DetectorConfig::refiner`) live at the top level of
`DetectorConfig` and apply to both strategies. Descriptors
always sample at the detector ring radius.

# Common knobs

- `ring` — choose the detector kernel radius.
- `center_of_mass` — tune the subpixel
  localizer.

center_of_mass.description:
ChESS's subpixel localizer: the response-weighted center of mass of
the response map around each integer peak. It gives every corner its
final position unless an image refiner
(`DetectorConfig::refiner`) is set;
the image refiner then starts from the integer peak instead.

ring.description:
Detector ring radius. `Canonical` selects the paper's `r=5`,
`Broad` selects `r=10`. Descriptors sample at this same radius.

ChessRing.description:
ChESS sampling ring radius. Selects the `r=5` (canonical) or `r=10`
(broad) ring used by the dense response kernel.

oneOf.description:
Radius-10 ring. Larger support window for callers that want the
detector to sample farther from the candidate center.

DetectionParams.description:
Shared non-maximum-suppression and peak-clustering thresholds.

These two knobs have identical meaning for the ChESS and Radon
detectors, so they live once at the `DetectorConfig` level rather
than being duplicated inside each strategy config. Both are expressed
in the detector's working-resolution pixels (for Radon, that is after
`image_upsample`). Tune them through
`DetectorConfig::with_detection`.

The defaults match the ChESS presets; the Radon presets raise
`nms_radius` to `4` to suit the wider Radon response peak.

min_cluster_size.description:
Minimum number of positive-response neighbours within the NMS
window that a candidate must have to be accepted (integer `>= 0`,
unitless count). Increase to suppress isolated noise peaks, at the
cost of possibly missing weak corners near image boundaries.

nms_radius.description:
Non-maximum-suppression half-radius, in working-resolution pixels
(integer `>= 0`). Only the highest-response pixel within this radius
is kept: reduce when corners are packed closer than `2·nms_radius`
pixels, increase to suppress near-duplicates on blurry images.

DetectionStrategy.description:
Top-level detector dispatch. Selects between the ChESS kernel
pipeline and the Radon whole-image detector. The chosen variant
carries all detector-specific tuning; settings that don't apply to
the active detector are simply unreachable, so the type system
enforces correctness instead of silently ignoring fields.

oneOf.description: ChESS kernel detection with optional coarse-to-fine multiscale.

ImageRefiner.description:
The optional image-refinement stage
(`DetectorConfig::refiner`).

Each detector first places its corners with its own subpixel localizer on
its response map: ChESS with the center of mass
(`ChessConfig::center_of_mass`),
Radon with the peak fit (`RadonConfig::peak_fit`).
An image refiner reads only the input image around each corner, so every
variant works with both detectors. Where it starts and what happens when
it cannot refine a corner follow the detector:

- **ChESS**: the refiner replaces the center of mass. It starts from the
  integer response peak, and a corner it rejects is dropped.
- **Radon**: the refiner runs on top of the peak fit. It starts from the
  peak-fit position, and a corner it does not refine to convergence keeps
  its peak-fit position. No corner is dropped.

Under `Uncertainty::Propagated` a
corner's position covariance comes from whichever localizer produced its
final position.

oneOf.description:
Quadratic surface fit to the image patch at the saddle point,
re-centred until it converges. Usually more accurate than the
detector's own localizer, most of all under lens blur and board
rotation; on cells of about 4 px its fit window spans the
neighbouring corners. Reports a position covariance on the corners it
refines to convergence.

MultiscaleConfig.description:
Coarse-to-fine multiscale configuration.

JSON shape mirrors `UpscaleConfig`:

- `"single_scale"` — run the detector once on the full image.
- `{ "pyramid": { "levels": 3, "min_size": 128, "refinement_radius": 3 } }`
  — build an image pyramid, detect seeds on the coarsest level, and
  refine each seed into the base image. Honoured by both ChESS and
  Radon strategies.

levels.description:
Number of pyramid levels (integer `>= 1`, at most 255). Level 0
is the base image; each subsequent level is a 2× box-filter
downsample.

min_size.description:
Minimum short-edge length of a pyramid level, in pixels. The
pyramid stops once the next level would fall below this size.

refinement_radius.description:
ROI half-radius at the coarse level used to refine each seed
into the base image, in coarse-level pixels (integer `>= 0`).

NoiseLevel.description:
The image noise level that turns a propagated position covariance into
px² (see `Uncertainty::Propagated`).

In JSON: `"estimate"` or `{"known": 1.2}`.

oneOf.description:
Estimate σ from each image with
`estimate_noise_sigma_u8` (the
default), once per frame and only when a corner carries a
covariance. The estimate is not reliable on demosaiced or JPEG
images; use `Known` for those.

A known standard deviation of the image's pixel noise, in gray
levels (finite and `>= 0`), for example the standard deviation of
the difference of two frames of a static scene, divided by `√2`.
It is the total noise as it appears in the 8-bit image, rounding
included (rounding adds `1/12` gray level² to the sensor noise,
which matters only below about 1 gray level). The covariance never
uses a variance below that `1/12`.

OrientationMethod.description:
Method used to fit the two grid axes at a detected corner.

`RingFit` is the default. `DiskFit` samples a larger
local support region and is intended for corners with strong
projective skew (axis separation far from 90°).

All variants emit `axes[0]` and `axes[1]` under the same canonical
convention documented on `CornerDescriptor`:
`axes[0].angle ∈ [0, π)`, `axes[1].angle ∈ (axes[0].angle,
axes[0].angle + π)`, and the CCW arc `(axes[0], axes[1])` is a *dark*
sector of the corner. Downstream consumers can therefore compare
`axes[0]` slot parity between corners regardless of which method
produced them.

oneOf.description:
Fit the parametric two-axis chessboard intensity model
`I(φ) = μ + A·tanh(β·sin(φ−θ₁))·tanh(β·sin(φ−θ₂))` to 16
ring samples via Gauss-Newton seeded from the 2nd-harmonic
orientation. Suspicious local minima are retried from a small
deterministic seed grid over the same 16 samples. When a
radius-10 detector ring is used and the fit still looks
suspicious, the canonical radius-5 ring is sampled as a cheap
safety check and used when it produces a valid contrast/residual
fit. Each axis reports the residual-scaled least-squares standard
error of this fit (`AxisEstimate::fit_std_error`).

This is the **default** method. Suitable for the full range of
standard chessboard images.

Full-disk crossing-line estimator. Samples all image pixels in a
disk around the corner center and fits two possibly non-orthogonal
axes from the resulting gradient field. When local evidence is
weak or the ring fit already indicates a clean orthogonal corner,
falls back to `RingFit` output transparently.

Use this when standard chessboards are imaged under strong
projective warp (axis separation far from 90°). It has higher
per-corner cost than `RingFit`; the lazy gate keeps the full disk
fit off clean orthogonal corners.

Output axes use the same canonical convention as `RingFit`
— see the type-level doc comment above and
`CornerDescriptor`. When the disk fit is used, each axis
reports its residual-scaled least-squares standard error over the
disk pixels; a ring-fit fallback reports the ring fit's, at least
10° when the two fits disagree.
Classic parabolic fit on the raw response values.

Parabolic fit on `log(response)` — equivalent to fitting a
Gaussian through three samples. This is the paper default and
the facade preset.

RadonConfig.description:
Configuration for the whole-image Radon detector branch of
`DetectionStrategy`.

All radii and counts are in **working-resolution** pixels (i.e.
after `image_upsample`). The shared NMS / clustering thresholds
(`DetectionParams`), multiscale, and upscale live at the top level
of `DetectorConfig` and apply to both strategies.

# Common knobs

- `image_upsample` — `2` (the default)
  reproduces the paper's 2× supersampled detection; `1` is faster but
  less accurate on low-resolution inputs.

# Advanced tuning

The remaining fields control low-level detection behaviour. The
defaults reproduce the paper's recommended settings and work well
for typical camera images. Adjust them only when you have a specific
reason (e.g. a non-standard image resolution or SNR budget).

image_upsample.description:
Image-level supersampling factor applied before ray integration
(`1` or `2`). `1` operates on the input grid; `2` (paper default)
bilinearly upsamples the input first, giving sub-pixel ray
positioning. The core detector clamps values outside `1..=2`.

peak_fit.description:
Advanced tuning. Radon's subpixel localizer: the 3-point fit of the
response-map argmax. `Gaussian` (default) fits on log-response (more
accurate near the peak); `Parabolic` fits directly on the response
values. See `PeakFitMode`. It gives every corner its final position
unless an image refiner
(`DetectorConfig::refiner`)
converges on it.

ray_radius.description:
Advanced tuning. Half-length of each Radon ray, in
working-resolution pixels (integer `>= 1`; the ray has
`2·ray_radius + 1` samples). Paper default at `image_upsample = 2`
is `4`. Shorter rays are faster but integrate less signal; longer
rays are more discriminating but may cross into neighbouring cells.

response_blur_radius.description:
Advanced tuning. Half-size of the box blur applied to the Radon
response map after integration, in working-resolution pixels
(integer `>= 0`). `0` disables blurring; the default `1` yields a
3×3 box that smooths quantisation noise.

SaddlePointConfig.description:
Configuration for the `SaddlePointRefiner`.

All thresholds below are advanced tuning knobs. The defaults are
appropriate for most scenes; adjust only if you observe excessive
rejection or acceptance of clearly-wrong refinements.

det_margin.description:
Margin on the Hessian determinant of the fitted quadratic
(unitless, `>= 0`): a saddle is confirmed only when
`det(H) < -det_margin`. Increase to require a sharper saddle.

Advanced tuning.

max_offset.description:
Maximum displacement from the seed to the fitted stationary point,
in pixels (`>= 0`); refinements that move farther are rejected.
The effective bound is also capped at `radius + 0.5`.

Advanced tuning.

min_abs_det.description:
Minimum absolute value of `det(H)` (unitless, `>= 0`). Rejects
near-flat surfaces whose determinant is too close to zero to be
meaningful.

Advanced tuning.

radius.description:
Half-size of the image patch used for the surface fit, in image
pixels (integer `>= 1`; the patch is `(2·radius+1)²`). Default `2`
(5×5 patch).

Advanced tuning.

Uncertainty.description:
Which position uncertainty each corner reports in
`position_covariance`.

Detector-independent: it applies to every localizer (the ChESS
refiners and the Radon peak fit) the same way. Corner positions are the
same under every variant.

In JSON: `"off"`, `{"propagated": {"noise": "estimate"}}` or
`{"propagated": {"noise": {"known": 1.2}}}`.

oneOf.description:
No position covariance (the default). Localizers skip the noise
propagation and the systematic model, and the detector makes no
noise estimate.

Image noise propagated through the localizer to first order, plus
the localizer's systematic-error model (from the corner's offset to
the localizer's fit window and the width of its edges). `noise` is
the image noise level that expresses the propagated part in px².

Every localizer reports a covariance. None is reported on upscaled
input (`DetectorConfig::upscale`):
interpolation correlates the noise of neighbouring pixels.

The systematic part includes a per-localizer floor measured on real
calibration images (about 0.05 px per axis for the saddle-point fit
and the Radon peak fit, 0.07 center of mass). On real, well-exposed
images this floor is usually the largest part of the covariance, so
the reported σ varies little from corner to corner there. Weighting
a calibration by it has not been shown to beat uniform weighting on
real data. Errors shared by all corners of an image (defocus,
lens-model error) are outside it. The floor was fitted on one camera
pair and is likely low for other optics. Within that pair the two
cameras' own floors differed by up to 2×.

UpscaleConfig.description:
Optional pre-pipeline integer-factor upscaling.

JSON shape mirrors the other enum-with-payload knobs
(`MultiscaleConfig`):

- `"disabled"` — no upscaling (default).
- `{ "fixed": 2 }` — upscale by an integer factor before detection.
  Allowed factors: `{2, 3, 4}`. Output corner coordinates are
  rescaled back to the original input-pixel frame by the facade.

oneOf.description: Upscale by a fixed integer factor (unitless; allowed: 2, 3, 4).

description:
High-level detection configuration.

Build one with `DetectorConfig::chess`,
`DetectorConfig::chess_multiscale`, `DetectorConfig::radon`, or
`DetectorConfig::radon_multiscale` and tweak only the fields you need.
The detector translates this into the low-level `ChessParams` /
`RadonDetectorParams` consumed by `chess-corners-core` at the detection
boundary.

# Common knobs

These fields are the primary surface for most callers:

- `strategy` — choose ChESS or Radon and
  configure its parameters.
- `threshold` — control how many corners are
  returned: lower → more candidates, higher → fewer and stronger. ChESS
  reads it as an absolute response floor; Radon as a fraction of the
  per-frame maximum.
- `multiscale` — enable coarse-to-fine
  pyramid detection (`Pyramid`) or keep it off (`SingleScale`).
- `upscale` — pre-pipeline integer bilinear
  upscaling for low-resolution inputs where corners have fewer than 5 px
  of ring support. `Disabled` by default.
- `refiner` — an optional image refiner that
  improves on the detector's own subpixel localizer. `None` by default.
- `orientation_method` — how corner
  axis orientations are estimated when building descriptors.
- `uncertainty` — whether each corner
  reports a position covariance, and the image noise level behind it.

# Advanced tuning

- `detection` — shared NMS / clustering
  thresholds applied by both strategies. See `DetectionParams`.
- `merge_radius` — duplicate-suppression
  radius across pyramid levels. See the field docs below.

# Deserialization

An omitted key takes its default, so `{}` is the default config. An
unknown key is an error that names it, at every level of the tree.

detection.description:
Shared non-maximum-suppression and peak-clustering thresholds.
Honoured by both strategies. See `DetectionParams`.

merge_radius.description:
Advanced tuning. Merge radius for cross-level and cross-seed
duplicate suppression, in base-image pixels (`>= 0`, default `3.0`).
After coarse-level seeds are refined into the base image, any two
refined positions within this radius are merged into one corner:
increase if you see duplicates of the same physical corner, decrease
if distinct corners closer than `2·merge_radius` pixels get merged.

multiscale.description:
Coarse-to-fine multiscale configuration. `SingleScale` skips
the pyramid entirely; `Pyramid` detects seeds on a coarse level and
refines them into the base image. Honoured by both strategies.

orientation_method.description:
Orientation-fit method used when building corner descriptors, or
`None` to skip the per-corner fit entirely. When `None`, every
descriptor carries `axes: None`; positions and responses are
unaffected. Skipping orientation is the cheaper path for consumers
that derive board geometry themselves.

refiner.description:
Image-refinement stage, or `None` (the default) to keep the
detector's own subpixel localizer: ChESS's center of mass, Radon's
peak fit. See `ImageRefiner` for where a refiner starts on each
detector and what it does with a corner it cannot refine.

strategy.description: Detector dispatch: ChESS or Radon, each carrying its own tuning.

threshold.description:
Detector acceptance threshold (`>= 0`).

ChESS reads it as an absolute floor on the raw response
`R = SR − DR − 16·MR`: a candidate is kept when `R` exceeds it.
Useful floors run roughly `30..=300` depending on image contrast;
the default is `30`, which suppresses texture noise while keeping
well-formed corners.
Radon reads it as a fraction in `[0.0, 1.0]` of the per-frame
maximum response, because Radon's `(max − min)²` score scales
with image size and has no portable absolute scale. On the
coarse-to-fine path the maximum is that of the strongest corner
found across the refinement windows.

uncertainty.description:
Which position uncertainty each corner reports in
`position_covariance`,
and the image noise level that expresses it in px². See
`Uncertainty`; `Uncertainty::Off` (the default) reports none and
makes no noise estimate.

upscale.description:
Pre-pipeline integer bilinear upscaling for low-resolution inputs.
`Disabled` skips the stage; `Fixed(k)` upscales by the unitless
factor `k` in `{2, 3, 4}`. Output coordinates stay in input pixels.
